title: theOS owns avenSANDBOX and the release pipeline
note: Ownership moved at once (D-24): avenDB's pipeline is parked; theOS's own box and release grow in checkpoints 2 and 3, after Gate A.

questions.q: Move avenSANDBOX into theOS (theOS owns it and its release from then on), or copy it and leave avenDB's release where it is? And who releases the box afterwards?
options: Copy it into theOS; avenDB keeps releasing until theOS's copy passes its gates (recommended: no release path changes before Gate A)
Move it: theOS owns it and its release now

questions.q: Gate A for AIP-2, after its spec review: are its claims, assumptions, outcome and mockup what must be true?
What does theOS release, and where?
options: theOS's apps as a site at aven.maia.city, in place of avenOS, once checkpoint 3 is green (recommended)
Nothing public yet: releases are versions on GitHub only

who: Samuel Andert, who wants one authority for what ships.
avenMAIA, which lives in the box: the cloud environment avenSANDBOX warms every new session with the box's image.
problem.experience: Every new session warms avenDB's box (Docker, four avenDB peers), which theOS does not use, while theOS has no box, workflow or release of its own; and what is released and served is defined by avenDB, a legacy project theOS must not change.

items.text: avensandbox.yml released avenOS, avenSANDBOX and avenPEER from production, each under a dated version; the last release is #1750 (avenOS 26.10.31v6, avenPEER 26.10.31v5, avenSANDBOX 26.10.31v2).
avensandbox-image.yml and avenpeer-image.yml built their images from aven/DB2's Cargo workspace.
avendeploy.yml deployed the avenCEO Peer and avenOS at aven.maia.city, by hand.
aven/DB2/sandbox/box/Dockerfile compiles avenDB's third-party crates; cloud-setup.sh runs avenDB's `bun run up`, four avenDB peers.
The environment's setup script looks only for aven/DB2/sandbox/box/cloud-setup.sh, and exits 0 when it is not there (aven/DB2/SANDBOX.md, "Samuel's part").

problem.baseline: Before the park: four workflows, all avenDB's. theOS has no box, no workflow and no release of its own.
whys: A new session warms a box theOS does not use, and theOS cannot ship. Why? The box and the pipeline build, test and release avenDB.
Why? They were built for avenDB (29 to 31 Oct) before theOS became the standalone project (D-4).
Root cause: the release pipeline and the sandbox belong to a legacy project.
truths: GitHub runs the workflow files of the branch an event happens on; a file moved out of .github/workflows/ on that branch never runs there.
A deployed server keeps serving what it was last given until something deploys again.
An image already published to a registry stays pullable when its workflow stops.
The environment's setup script never fails a session: it exits 0 when it finds no setup file.
A workflow file must live in .github/workflows/; what it runs can live in theOS/.
assumptions: Nothing depends on a new avenDB release; aven.maia.city may stay as it is until theOS releases.
theOS's checks need only bun, Chromium and Playwright now; Lean, Rust and the vectors join when an AIP needs them.
Changing the environment's setup script is a setting only you can change; you paste it at Gate B, when you try it.
problem.risk: Can be undone: the park by moving the four files back (.github/workflows-avendb/README.md); the setup script by switching the environment's script back. The environment's script is shared by every session in it; nothing in theOS relies on avenDB's warm box. production's ruleset requires two checks only the parked workflow reported, so nothing merges into production until theOS releases.

reuse.use: Learned from: production takes changes from main only; one release per changed package, under the date (26.10.29, 26.10.29v2, ...); a push that changes nothing releases nothing.
Learned from: the image is tagged by the hash of the files its build reads, so every checkout runs exactly its own box; built per architecture, then joined.

reuse.what: aven/DB2/sandbox/box/cloud-setup.sh and the environment's setup script
reuse.use: Learned from: warm the box once, before the disk is snapshotted; never fail a session.
Learned from: run by hand in the environment production; health checks after the deploy; nothing secret printed, the repository is public.

claims.promise: Once the park is on main and production, no avenDB workflow runs there, and nothing live changes: aven.maia.city keeps answering, and the published box and peer images stay pullable. Branches made before the park keep their copies until they merge main.
claims.fails: A parked workflow still runs on main or production, or the park takes something down.
claims.check: After the merge: the Actions runs of main and production show none of the four; aven.maia.city answers; a new cloud session starts.

claims.promise: A new cloud session warms theOS's box, not avenDB's, and a session whose warm-up fails or hangs still starts.
claims.fails: A setup error or a hang stops every new session before Claude starts.
claims.check: theOS/sandbox/setup.sh, run in a copy with a planted failure and with a planted hang, exits 0 within its time limit; after you paste the environment's script at Gate B, a new session starts with theOS's box warm.

claims.promise: theOS's box is set up only from files in theOS/: theOS/sandbox/setup.sh installs from theOS's lockfile, and theOS's check command (AIP-1, checkpoint 1) runs green after it.
claims.fails: The box needs files outside theOS/, or the check passes outside the box and fails in it.
claims.check: In a checkout that holds only theOS/, run the setup script, then the check.

outcome.promise: A new session reaches a green theOS check with no avenDB warm-up.
outcome.how: The first session after Gate B, read off its setup log and the check's report.

checkpoints.adds: avenDB's four workflows parked in .github/workflows-avendb/, with a README and a note atop the repository's CLAUDE.md. Done at your direct ask (D-24), commit 2d6f53842.
theOS/sandbox/setup.sh: warms theOS's box, never fails or hangs a session; the environment's new setup script, for you to paste at Gate B.
After AIP-1's checkpoint 1: the setup script installs from theOS's lockfile and runs theOS's check.
